name: Testosterone cypionate

lead: Testosterone cypionate is a slow-release injectable ester of testosterone used to treat low testosterone and in masculinizing hormone therapy. Its labelled virilizing effects include deeper voice, body and facial hair growth, and acne.

The ester is released slowly and converted to testosterone, which activates the androgen receptor, including in laryngeal tissue. Voice change is a side effect of androgen action rather than a studied purpose, and no trials test it for appearance goals. Non-medical use for physique and performance is reported as common.

paras: Clinically it is prescribed for confirmed deficiency or gender-affirming care under medical supervision with regular monitoring. Effects such as body-composition and voice changes develop gradually over months.

Labelled risks include acne, hair loss, fertility suppression, cardiovascular events, clotting, polycythemia concerns and contraindication in pregnancy. It is a Schedule III controlled substance in the US, and voice changes in women may be permanent.

angle.text: Testosterone cypionate is a long-acting injectable labelled for hypogonadism, and its androgen action on the larynx deepens the voice. That deepening is a listed virilizing effect rather than a studied purpose.

lead: Testosterone cypionate is a long-acting injectable ester of testosterone, sold mainly as Depo-Testosterone, and a prodrug the body converts to testosterone. It is FDA-labelled for replacement therapy in males with primary or hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.[1][2][3]

Its listed virilizing effects include acne, body and facial hair growth and deepening of the voice.[1] It is a Schedule III controlled substance in the US, and non-medical use for physique and performance is reported as common.[1]
infobox: About 7 to 8 days after intramuscular injection[1]
US Schedule III; Canada Schedule IV[1]

paras: The US label lists replacement therapy in men with testicular failure or pituitary-hypothalamic disorders. It is also used in masculinizing hormone therapy for transgender men, and off-label for several other conditions.[1][3]
A 12-month randomized trial in older hypogonadal men examined testosterone replacement effects on physical and cognitive decline.[4]

The label lists gynecomastia, oligospermia at high doses, hirsutism, male-pattern baldness, acne, fluid retention, liver test changes, and reports of myocardial infarction, stroke and venous thromboembolism. It is contraindicated in pregnancy because it can virilize a female fetus.[3]
A placebo-controlled crossover trial of supraphysiologic testosterone cypionate in healthy men studied effects on mood and aggression.[5]
It is the cyclopentylpropionate ester of testosterone (C27H40O3), converted slowly to testosterone, which acts at the androgen receptor and may convert to DHT or estradiol.[1]
Wikipedia notes marketing mainly in the US and non-medical use for physique enhancement. Voice deepening is among the effects reported with androgen use.[1]

Randomized trials include a 12-month study in hypogonadal older men and a placebo-controlled study of mood and aggression with supraphysiologic dosing; registered trials include a phase 3 weekly auto-injector study in hypogonadal men and several studies in prostate cancer.[4][5][6][7] No study was found evaluating it for voice change.

timeline.event: Synthesized and introduced in the US as Depo-Testosterone.[1]
